class.name: PhysXBlastAsset
class.brief_description: A fractured mesh, ready to drive a [PhysXDestructible3D].
class.description: Produced by the in-editor [b]Mesh → Fracture with Blast[/b] dialog (or [PhysXBlastAuthoring] directly, for scripted/offline authoring), and saved as a normal [code].tres[/code]/[code].res[/code] file next to the scene. Assign it to a [PhysXDestructible3D]'s [member PhysXDestructible3D.blast_asset] to use it -- there's nothing to configure on the asset itself once it's authored.

method.name: get_chunk_count
method.description: Returns how many chunks this asset has, including chunk [code]0[/code] (the whole unfractured mesh) -- so this is always one more than the number of pieces a full fracture actually produces.

method.name: prepare_render
method.description: Converts every chunk's render arrays to GPU format now, the costly part of building them, so a [PhysXDestructible3D] using this asset later only uploads them instead of stalling the frame it spawns or splits in. Safe to call from a worker thread (for example with [WorkerThreadPool]) while nothing edits the asset. The chunk meshes are built once and shared by every destructible using this asset; calling it again does nothing.

members.member: The raw NvBlast asset data (bond/chunk support-graph structure) -- a single relocatable memory block per NvBlast's own design, stored here as-is. Not meaningful to edit by hand.

Optional initial health of each bond, in the asset's own bond order, as a multiple of [member PhysXDestructible3D.health]: a thin joint such as [code]0.01[/code] breaks long before a thick one such as [code]50[/code]. [method PhysXBlastAuthoring.build_prefractured] fills it from each bond's [code]health[/code]. When this is empty, or its size doesn't match the bond count, every bond starts at [member PhysXDestructible3D.health].

Optional collision hulls, one [PackedVector3Array] of convex hull points per chunk (a few dozen points). [PhysXDestructible3D] cooks these instead of every triangle corner in [member chunk_points], which makes spawning pieces much cheaper. When this is empty, hulls are made from [member chunk_points].

Optional render meshes, one [Mesh] arrays [Array] per chunk (indexed or not), for chunks authored with their own shading data (see [method PhysXBlastAuthoring.build_prefractured]). [PhysXDestructible3D] draws pieces with their normals, tangents, colours and UVs. When this is empty, pieces are drawn from [member chunk_points] with flat normals. For a chunk with several materials (bark, wood, moss, leaves), an entry may also be a [Mesh], or an [Array] of surfaces, each a [Mesh] arrays [Array] or a [Dictionary] with [code]arrays[/code] and [code]slot[/code]. Each surface is drawn with [member materials][code][slot][/code]; a surface's slot is its index unless given, and a [Mesh] surface whose material is in [member materials] takes that material's slot. A piece's mesh gets one surface per slot, whatever number of chunks it carries.

Per-chunk render-mesh triangle-soup positions, in the source mesh's local space -- one [PackedVector3Array] per chunk, index-matched to [member asset_bytes]' own chunk indices. Not meaningful to edit by hand.
Materials by surface slot for [member chunk_meshes]. [member PhysXDestructible3D.material_override], when set, covers all of them.
